title: Heading at Beginning of Print Page

illustrates.quote: Insert a blank line after the page change indicator when the new print page starts with a format that normally is preceded by a blank line. (See Sample 1-2: Heading at Beginning of Print Page on page 1-22.)

page.features: New print page number 325 ('#cbe': c=3,b=2,e=5), shown at the page turn; the preceding page's own number is not itself given in this excerpt.

blocks.text: Others have special structures on their back in which their young develop.
blocks.features: Final sentence ending the previous print page.
Centred heading opening the new print page.

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered what happens to frogs and toads in the winter when the temperature falls?
blocks.features: Opening paragraph following the heading, indented first line.

braille.notes: Braille page lines 4-11 of the source, renumbered from 1. Line 3 (source line 6) is the full-width page-change indicator ending '#cbe' (325). A blank line follows it (per 1.11.3.c, since the heading that opens the new print page would normally itself be preceded by a blank line) -- the rule this sample illustrates; the centred heading follows; another blank line precedes the paragraph per the ordinary heading-then-paragraph spacing rule; the paragraph resumes on the last two lines.

resolution: Both runs agree on wording and the underlying mechanic (both cite 1.11.3.c). Confirmed 'Others' (not 'Otters', a prior reference index's own error) directly against the source .txt and cross-checked by both independent runs. Structural choice: a leading 'paragraph', mid-flow 'pagenum' block, centred 'heading', then a closing 'paragraph' -- verified empirically against Emboss (gold-run.mjs scratch probe): this exact block sequence reproduces the given braille.lines byte-for-byte (aside from the established letter-case convention, standards-findings.md F-24) -- this sample is expected to MATCH.
